statement: For an absolutely continuous probability distribution with probability density function f(x), the differential entropy h(X) (also written h(f)) is defined by h(X) = -\int f(x) \log f(x) \, dx. The supplied sources contain no derivation of differential entropy itself, as it is introduced as a definition generalizing Shannon entropy to continuous distributions; the derivation under the Proof heading in the source derives a property (maximization under a normal distribution) rather than the definition itself.

properties.property: Translation invariance: h(X + c) = h(X) for a constant c.
properties.why: Rigid translations have a Jacobian determinant equal to 1.

properties.property: Scalar scaling: h(aX) = h(X) + \log |a| for a constant a.
properties.why: Linear scaling by a multiplies the density volume element by the absolute Jacobian determinant |a|.

properties.property: Linear transformation: h(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{X}) = h(\mathbf{X}) + \log(|\det \mathbf{A}|) for an invertible square matrix \mathbf{A}.
properties.why: The multi-dimensional density transforms under linear maps by scaling with the absolute determinant of \mathbf{A}.

properties.property: General coordinate transformation bound: h(\mathbf{Y}) \le h(\mathbf{X}) + \int f(x) \log |\frac{\partial m}{\partial x}| \, dx for \mathbf{Y} = m(\mathbf{X}), with equality if m is a bijection.
properties.why: Under coordinate transformation m the density transforms via the Jacobian determinant |\partial m / \partial x|.

properties.property: Invariance under rigid motions: h(Y) = h(X) when m is a rigid rotation, translation, or combination thereof.
properties.why: The Jacobian determinant of any rigid motion is identically 1.

properties.property: Conditioning reduces entropy: h(X | Y) \le h(X) with equality if and only if X and Y are independent.
properties.why: Mutual information satisfies I(X; Y) \ge 0 with equality iff X and Y are independent.

properties.property: Chain rule: h(X_1, \ldots, X_n) = \sum_{i=1}^n h(X_i | X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}) \le \sum_{i=1}^n h(X_i).
properties.why: Successive decomposition of joint continuous entropy via conditional differential entropies.

properties.property: Maximization by Gaussian distribution: For zero-mean \mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with covariance matrix K, h(\mathbf{X}) \le \frac{1}{2} \log(\det(2\pi e K)) = \frac{1}{2}\log[(2\pi e)^n \det K], with equality iff \mathbf{X} is jointly Gaussian.
properties.why: Kullback-Leibler divergence D_{KL}(f \parallel g) \ge 0 between an arbitrary distribution f and Gaussian g of equal covariance.

properties.property: Estimator error lower bound: \operatorname{E}[(X - \widehat{X})^2] \ge \frac{1}{2\pi e} e^{2h(X)} for any estimator \widehat{X}, with equality iff X is Gaussian and \widehat{X} is its mean.
properties.why: Differential entropy provides an information-theoretic lower bound on expected squared estimation error.

properties.property: Sign variability: Differential entropy can be negative.
properties.why: Continuous probability density functions can exceed 1 over regions of their support.

properties.property: Discrete quantization connection: A quantized variable X_h = ih with bin width h has discrete entropy H_h = -\sum_i h f(ih) \log(f(ih)) - \sum h f(ih) \log(h), where the first term approximates h(X) and the second approximates -\log(h).
properties.why: Partitioning the continuous range into intervals of length h separates the Riemann sum approximating h(X) from the divergent bin-width term.

assumptions.assumption: The random variable or vector possesses an absolutely continuous probability distribution admitting a probability density function f(x).
assumptions.breaks_when: The distribution has discrete point masses or singular components lacking a density with respect to Lebesgue measure.

assumptions.assumption: The density f(x) satisfies integrability conditions such that -\int f(x) \log f(x) \, dx converges.
assumptions.breaks_when: The distribution has pathological heavy tails or severe local singularities causing the integral to diverge.

assumptions.assumption: The transformation matrix \mathbf{A} is invertible and square.
assumptions.breaks_when: \det \mathbf{A} = 0, which collapses the dimension and renders the distribution non-absolutely continuous in \mathbb{R}^n.

assumptions.assumption: The vector transformation m is a bijection for entropy equality.
assumptions.breaks_when: m is not bijective (many-to-one or non-invertible), yielding only an inequality.

failure_modes.signature: Entropy changes value or sign under change of units or linear scaling: h(aX) = h(X) + \log |a|.
failure_modes.cause: Differential entropy lacks an invariant measure factor, making it non-invariant under arbitrary coordinate transformations.
The probability density function f(x) exceeds 1 over a significant portion of its support, causing \log f(x) > 0.

failure_modes.signature: Entropy transformation formula produces -\infty due to \log |\det \mathbf{A}| when \det \mathbf{A} = 0.
failure_modes.cause: Singular matrix \mathbf{A} reduces the dimensionality of the random vector.
